signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: The G10 Currency Scorecard registers a 3.468% leader-to-laggard spread, driven by CHF 1W outperformance (+1.232% avg across 6 pairs) against heavy AUD weakness (-2.236% avg across 4 pairs). AUD/CHF trades at 0.5627 while holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5640–0.5748, confirming technical alignment with the downside. Safe-haven capital allocation into CHF accelerates following reports of two oil tankers catching fire in the Strait of Hormuz, directly pressuring growth-sensitive commodity currencies. A massive 485bp rate differential (RBA 4.85% vs SNB 0.00%) offers little support as risk-off flows dominate carry considerations while VIX remains elevated at 28.2. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, driven by safe-haven capital flows. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp geopolitical de-escalation that triggers a rapid risk-on unwind into high-carry currencies.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Crowded Carry + Risk Reversal Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.92, holding below its 20-day SMA at 157.95 while remaining above the 50-day SMA at 157.33 within a tight 20-session box structure. The 275bp rate spread (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and 271bp OIS carry advantage maintain structural support for the dollar, yet 25d Risk Reversals indicate a strong put skew of -1.80, signaling that institutional options markets are paying up for downside protection. CFTC data shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short at -19,224 contracts (94th percentile of its 52-week range, z=+1.57), revealing crowded carry positioning vulnerable to sudden liquidations. Japan real wages accelerating to 2.2% reinforces the BoJ tightening outlook, tightening the squeeze potential if equity market volatility spills over. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; crowded carry positioning clashes with options downside hedging. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls report at 13:30 UTC. Risk: US NFP beat that drives US Treasury yields higher and overwhelms downside option hedging.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Divergence + Retail Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5560, maintaining a bearish posture below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5642, 0.5703, and 0.5825. Economic data continues to deteriorate sharply with the NZD Economic Surprise Index printing at -25.1, while retail traders have pushed positioning to an extreme 88% long. This extreme retail long stance directly diverges from institutional CFTC positioning, where Leveraged Funds hold a net short of -22,722 contracts. With a 125bp carry advantage favoring the dollar (Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75%), fundamental data and institutional flows support further downside despite retail attempt to catch a falling trend. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; weak macroeconomic data and institutional net shorts favor trend continuation. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Retail capitulation triggering a temporary short-covering rally back toward the 20-day SMA at 0.5642.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility Complacency + Rate Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6882, remaining trapped in a clear downtrend below its falling 20-day SMA of 0.6997 and 200-day SMA of 0.7060. Options pricing exhibits notable complacency, with 1M ATM Implied Volatility at 6.2% against a 30-day Realized Volatility of 7.8%, generating a negative Volatility Risk Premium of -1.6%. A 85bp rate advantage (RBA 4.85% vs Fed 4.00%) and -91bp OIS spread favor AUD, but equity sell-offs and global growth concerns continue to suppress capital flows into the pair. According to model fair value metrics, AUD/USD trades cheap at a BEER misvaluation z-score of -2.67σ, pointing to long-term mean-reversion potential once cross-asset vol settles. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; negative VRP and technical downtrend outweigh the nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Rapid mean-reversion toward fair value triggered by a dovish US wage growth print.
